title: Zeitai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Meir’s son-in-law, as stated in Yuchasin. Seder HaDorot writes: “I have not found it.” Hyman endorses Yuchasin: in [Kohelet Rabbah 9:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.9.8.1), Zeitai says in Rabbi Meir’s name: “These recline and eat and drink, whereas those recline and do not eat.” [Shabbat 153a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.153a.8) attributes this saying to Rabbi Meir’s son-in-law in Rabbi Meir’s name. The Yalkut on Kohelet there explicitly names “Zeitai, Rabbi Meir’s son-in-law.”[^1]

notes.text: The Midrash names Zivtai as transmitting the teaching in Rabbi Meir’s name. The Bavli attributes the parallel teaching to Rabbi Meir’s unnamed son-in-law. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1113&lang=en) says that he found the Shabbat passage without the name Zivtai. Hyman compares the two passages to support the identification he takes from Yuchasin. Hyman also cites a named reading in the Yalkut.
